stem: A child with gastroenteritis is assessed as more than 5% dehydrated; which fluid replacement plan best matches usual prescribing practice?

options.text: Calculate rehydration fluids at 5% dehydration over the first 24 hours, then replace the remainder over the next 24 hours
Replace the entire assessed deficit in the first 24 hours regardless of size
Give maintenance only for 24 hours, then start replacing the deficit
Replace only the portion above 5% and ignore the first 5%
Delay deficit replacement until a premorbid weight is available

explanation: Calculate rehydration fluids at 5% dehydration over 24 hours, then replace any remaining deficit over the next 24 hours. This staged approach is the usual prescribing method for a child assessed as more than 5% dehydrated.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because usual prescribing is based on replacing 5% dehydration in the first 24 hours, then the remaining deficit over the following 24 hours.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the full deficit is not usually replaced in the first 24 hours when dehydration is more than 5%.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because maintenance fluids alone do not address the dehydration deficit in the initial management plan.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the first 5% is included in the standard replacement plan rather than being ignored.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because lack of a premorbid weight does not prevent percentage-based deficit replacement planning.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
